title: Inside Google's US$15bn Data Centre Strategy for Malaysia
summary: Google invests $15 billion in new data centre strategy across Malaysia
detailed: Google committed US$15bn to data centre infrastructure in Malaysia spanning 2027 to 2028, adding over 1GW of clean energy to the national grid.
The investment establishes new facilities in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan, following the operational launch of its first campus at Elmina Business Park.
Google operates its data center campuses at an energy-efficient Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of 1.12 to 1.14.
The construction is projected to contribute an annual average of US$1.1 billion to GDP and support over 37,000 jobs per year.
sentences: Google has committed US$15bn to Malaysia's data centre infrastructure over 2027 to 2028, combining energy-efficient campus development with plans to add more than 1GW of clean energy to the national grid.
Announced in the presence of Prime Minister YAB Dato' Seri Anwar bin Ibrahim, the investment establishes new facilities in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan industrial zones.
Google's first campus at Elmina Business Park, which broke ground in October 2024, is also now operational.
Additional sites have been planned to power services across Malaysia and the Asia-Pacific region, including its upcoming cloud region for enterprise customers.
Ruth Porat , President and Chief Investment Officer at Alphabet and Google, says: "Google is committed to growing our presence responsibly, delivering lasting value for Malaysia's economy and people.

"This investment aligns with Malaysia's development priorities – providing the foundational computing capacity to deliver the upside of innovation across the country while adding local power and water resources as our operations scale.
Google is proud to partner with local suppliers to expand their expertise and to equip workers, students and entrepreneurs with in-demand skills.
Custom-designed networking equipment, coolant systems and specialised chips enable this performance in tropical climates.
YB Gobind Singh Deo, Minister of Digital of Malaysia, says: "Google's comprehensive blueprint sets a high standard for sustainable, high-impact digital infrastructure development in Malaysia.

"Guided by the Malaysia MADANI framework and the Malaysia Digital 2030 Action Plan, our goal is to cultivate an ecosystem that strengthens Malaysia's technological capabilities, protects public resources and empowers our people.
Once operational, the company says facilities will sustain more than 9,000 jobs annually at wages 45% above the national median.
Furthermore, four training programmes by Google aim to upskill 800,000 Malaysian people by 2031.
Google employs data-driven water risk assessments before implementing cooling systems.
Projects with Global Environment Centre deploy constructed wetlands for Sungai Buloh and Sungai Selangor river basins, whilst school-based initiatives install rainwater harvesting systems.

Tenaga Nasional Berhad: Malaysia's national utility partners with Google to develop clean energy generation under the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme, exploring round-the-clock projects addressing solar intermittency whilst Google pays for power consumption and grid connection infrastructure.

Global Environment Centre: Delivers nature-based water solutions including floating wetland cells at Taman Aman Lake and river basin stewardship deploying constructed wetlands, bioengineering and pollution monitoring across Sungai Buloh and Sungai Selangor watersheds improving water quality.

Pepper Labs: Collaborates on Jelajah AI MSME, delivering clinics for microentrepreneurs across Selangor and Negeri Sembilan at NADI centres, leveraging grassroots digital training experience to help small businesses create searchable online profiles and digital storefronts.

Arus Academy: Partners on AKAD Rakyat training council officers across 19 local government councils in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan, appointing AI champions to modernise workflows and automate routine paperwork for more responsive public service delivery.

Shizen Energy-Solarvest: The consortium supports grid resilience and decarbonisation contributing to Google's 1 GW clean energy commitment for Malaysia's national grid, working alongside partnerships with Tenaga Nasional Berhad and TotalEnergies-led consortiums.
